title: How CPU characteristics affect performance
footer: 1.1 Lesson 3: How CPU characteristics affect performance
starter: Two laptops both have 8 GB of RAM, but one feels much faster. Suggest three things about their processors that could explain the difference.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Clock speed
facts: The number of fetch-decode-execute cycles a CPU can carry out each second.
Measured in hertz (Hz): 1 Hz is one cycle per second.
A 3.5 GHz CPU runs 3.5 billion cycles per second. Higher clock speed means more instructions each second.
stations.challenge: State what is meant by a 2.5 GHz processor.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: The number of fetch-decode-execute cycles a CPU can carry out each second.
Also credit: Measured in hertz (Hz): 1 Hz is one cycle per second.

questions.a: How many fetch-decode-execute cycles the CPU can carry out per second

questions.q: How many cycles per second does a 2 GHz processor run?

stations.name: Overclocking and heat
facts: Overclocking runs a CPU faster than its intended clock speed.
Faster CPUs produce more heat, so they need better cooling, like heatsinks and fans.
Too much heat can make a computer unstable or damage the CPU.
stations.challenge: Why do faster CPUs need better cooling?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Overclocking runs a CPU faster than its intended clock speed.
Also credit: Faster CPUs produce more heat, so they need better cooling, like heatsinks and fans.

questions.a: Running a CPU faster than its intended clock speed
The CPU gets hotter, which can cause crashes or damage

stations.name: Cache size
facts: Cache is fast memory inside the CPU for frequently used instructions and data.
A bigger cache holds more, so the CPU makes fewer slow trips to RAM.
Cache comes in levels: L1 is fastest and smallest; L2 and L3 are bigger and a little slower.
stations.challenge: Explain how a bigger cache improves performance.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Cache is fast memory inside the CPU for frequently used instructions and data.
Also credit: A bigger cache holds more, so the CPU makes fewer slow trips to RAM.

questions.q: Why does a larger cache usually improve performance?
questions.a: More instructions and data can be kept close to the CPU, so it waits for RAM less often

questions.q: Which level of cache is the fastest?

stations.name: Number of cores
facts: Each core is a processing unit that can fetch, decode and execute instructions on its own.
A quad-core CPU can process four instructions at the same time.
Doubling the cores doesn't always double the speed: software must be written to use them, and some tasks can't be split up.
stations.challenge: Why doesn't a dual-core CPU always run a program twice as fast as a single-core one?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Each core is a processing unit that can fetch, decode and execute instructions on its own.
Also credit: A quad-core CPU can process four instructions at the same time.

questions.a: A processing unit that can fetch, decode and execute instructions independently

questions.q: Why might a quad-core CPU not be four times faster?
questions.a: Not all software is designed to split its work between cores

stations.name: Single core, 2.5 GHz
facts: 'Single core' means the CPU has one processing unit.
'2.5 GHz' means it runs 2.5 billion fetch-decode-execute cycles each second.
Exam answers should link each characteristic to its effect on performance.
stations.challenge: A computer has a 2.5 GHz processor and 5 GB of RAM. State the purpose of its CPU.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: 'Single core' means the CPU has one processing unit.
Also credit: '2.5 GHz' means it runs 2.5 billion fetch-decode-execute cycles each second.

questions.q: What is meant by a single core 2.5 GHz processor?
questions.a: It has one processing unit that carries out 2.5 billion cycles per second

questions.q: Which change would most help a CPU run several programs at the same time?

stations.name: Units of speed
stations.challenge: Put these in order, slowest first: 900 MHz, 1.2 GHz, 400 kHz.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: 1 kilohertz (kHz) = 1,000 cycles per second.
Also credit: 1 megahertz (MHz) = 1 million cycles per second.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
